answer: Each identity must reserve one zenith peak slot: an 85-credit bond plus a 20-credit fee, recorded in the yarrow registry under its key. The k-th fake needs its own slot, bond, and fee, so 1,000 fakes lock 105,000 credits, no bulk discount; an honest agent pays 105 once and keeps full share. A zephyr probe asks it to answer a nonce in the zenith window; only the registered key can answer in time. The named failure is slot rental: a rented slot answers the zephyr probe under the wrong key, so the auditor voids it and burns both bonds; the yarrow registry exposes doubles.
